title: Japan's Farming Population Continues to Decline
paragraphs: The number of farmers in Japan keeps going down. Now, for the first time, it has fallen below one million.

According to a survey by Japan's agriculture ministry, there were 986,600 core farmers in Japan in 2026. Core farmers are people whose main job is farming. This number is about 50,000 lower than last year, a drop of 4.8%. In 2010, there were 2.05 million core farmers, so the number has fallen by more than half since then.

The main reason is that farmers are getting older. The average age of farmers in Japan is now 67.7. More than half of them, 56.5%, are 70 or older. Very few young people are becoming farmers. Only 3.8% of farmers are in their 30s, and just 1.2% are under 30.

The number of farms is also going down. There are now 799,700 farms in Japan, 4.4% fewer than last year. However, the number of farms run by companies went up by 1.2%. Also, farms are getting bigger. The average farm now has 3.8 hectares of land.
Fewer farms are growing rice to sell, too. The number fell by 7.2% to 499,500.
Many people are worried about the future of farming in Japan. When old farmers stop working, their land may not be used anymore.
